3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The morning after my coronation, I was woken up by a knock on the door.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: The door opened, and Pabel gracefully stepped in.

12.speaker: Pabel Adria
12.text: "You said you wanted to be woken up at this time, Your Majesty."

13.speaker: Player_Romus
13.text: "What nerve. Barge in on the King again like that, and I'll have your head."

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "It's nice to see a familiar face."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "Yes, I did. It's best to get a head start while the day's still young."

17.speaker: Player_Romus
17.text: "I knew this day would come, but it still feels odd having you wait on me."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "What nerve. Barge in on me again like that, and I'll have your head."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: The corner of Pabel's mouth twitched. He responded calmly.

23.speaker: Pabel Adria
23.text: "I wasn't informed you wanted one, Your Majesty. I'll make sure to bring you the Herald every morning going forward."

25.speaker: Pabel Adria
25.text: "You had better get used to it. Everyone answers to you now."

26.speaker: Player_Romus
26.text: "Sorry, I couldn't resist. How are you, Pabel?"

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: Pabel paused for a second, then responded with composure.

30.speaker: Pabel Adria
30.text: "Indeed. You've got a packed schedule ahead of you today."

32.speaker: Pabel Adria
32.text: "They're just getting it ready for you downstairs now."

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Pabel leveled his gaze at me, his manner calm.

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "No, no, I was joking. How are you, Pabel?"

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: In the eastern dining room, an enormous breakfast spread had been laid out.

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: My mother was already sitting at the table, digging a spoon into a single grapefruit half.

41.speaker: Player_Romus
41.text: "You're supposed to rise when the King enters the room."

42.speaker: Estela Toras
42.text: "How do you think I stay this trim, darling?"

44.speaker: Estela Toras
44.text: "I gave birth to you, darling, I've earned the right to stay seated."

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: Despite the early hour, my mother was already in her full makeup. She dabbed at her lips with a napkin.

46.speaker: Estela Toras
46.text: "That was one cheeky speech you gave yesterday. The papers are having a field day."

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "Forget the papers. Did you see the look on Hugo's face?"

53.speaker: Estela Toras
53.text: "I hope you're satisfied with yesterday's coronation. Your father's wasn't nearly as well-attended."

58.speaker: Estela Toras
58.text: "You ought to be careful, though. This country takes its royal traditions seriously."

59.speaker: Estela Toras
59.text: "Your father and I learned that the hard way."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "What can I say? My people love me."

63.speaker: Estela Toras
63.text: "They love to be seen on television. You, they're not so sure about."

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: My daughter gave a kiss on the cheek to mother, then me.

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: My daughter kissed mother on the cheek, then gave me a shy wave.

69.speaker: Player_Romus
69.text: "That's nonsense. Vina, eat as much as you want."

70.speaker: Player_Romus
70.text: "Absolutely. If you eat this much every morning, you'll never get married."

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: Vina took a bite of a rizetta and gave an exaggerated sigh of pleasure. My mother rolled her eyes.

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: Vina's smile vanished. She took most of the food off her plate.

74.speaker: Vina Toras
74.text: "Father, I wanted to ask you something."

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: It took me a few seconds to remember where I was.

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: The knocking on the door continued.

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: The door swung open. Pabel walked in, beaming.

78.speaker: Estela Toras
78.text: "Yes, better a dead wife than a common one."

79.speaker: Estela Toras
79.text: "Don't speak ill of the dead. Only their widows can do that."

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "That's only because of the TV cameras."

83.speaker: Estela Toras
83.text: "What was in that letter he wrote you, by the way? I never asked."

87.speaker: Estela Toras
87.text: "What did he say to you before he died, by the way? I never asked."

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "He said not to make the same mistakes he did."

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "He told me to take back the lands that were lost."

91.speaker: Estela Toras
91.text: "Zille and Pales, I suppose. He never did give up on the Grand Duchy."

92.speaker: Estela Toras
92.text: "He must've been talking about Zille and Pales. His great follies."

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: She handed me a rizetta, the traditional rice and quince custard tart. The crust was exceptionally flaky.

95.speaker: Vina Toras
95.text: "I nearly got lost on the way here. Grandma, why didn't you tell me this place had such a big library?"

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Vina eagerly took a plate and started piling it high with pastries. My mother clicked her tongue disapprovingly.

97.speaker: Estela Toras
97.text: "Not too many of those. The sweeter the taste, the wider the waist. Don't you agree, Romus?"

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "It's a special occasion. Our diet can start tomorrow."

101.speaker: Player_Romus
101.text: "I know. We're already behind on finding you a husband."

102.speaker: Player_Romus
102.text: "I know. You've got to start thinking about where to study."

103.speaker: Player_Romus
103.text: "Yes, it's time you started taking on more responsibilities."

106.speaker: Vina Toras
106.text: "That's not quite what I had in mind."

107.speaker: Vina Toras
107.text: "That was supposed to be a joke, right?"

108.speaker: Vina Toras
108.text: "I was thinking I'm old enough to accompany you to your council meetings."

109.speaker: Player_Romus
109.text: "No, getting an education was far more important to me."

116.speaker: Player_Romus
116.text: "No, learning how to fight for my country was far more important to me."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "Yes, but I had to keep my mouth shut."

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: "The council is no place for a princess."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "Well, 18 is old enough to get involved in royal politics."

120.speaker: Vina Toras
120.text: "And Lyza the Great is a huge legacy for me to live up to."

121.speaker: Vina Toras
121.text: "Well, this is what's important to me. Lyza the Great is a huge legacy to live up to, after all."

122.speaker: Vina Toras
122.text: "Please, Father. If I'm going to live up to the legacy of Lyza the Great, I need to start early."

123.speaker: Vina Toras
123.text: "So will I. I'm willing to make sacrifices to live up to the legacy of Lyza the Great."

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: "Yes, but they were too dull to bear."

125.speaker: Vina Toras
125.text: "It seems fascinating to me. And if I'm going to live up to the legacy of Lyza the Great, I'm going to have to start early."

126.speaker: Player_Romus
126.text: "All right, Vina. You can come to the meetings."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "Sorry, but your grandma's right. You'd get bored in those meetings anyway."

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "Your grandmother's just jealous, Vina. You can join the meetings if you want."

129.speaker: Player_Romus
129.text: "You're not coming to council meetings, Vina. That's an order."

131.speaker: Vina Toras
131.text: "I guess I'll just go read in my room, then."

135.speaker: Vina Toras
135.text: "Thank you! I can't wait to start. Oh, I'd better refresh myself on Rizian law."

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: She pushed her plate away and trudged back upstairs. Once she was gone, my mother lit a cigarette.

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: She pushed her plate away and dashed back up the stairs. Once she was gone, my mother lit a cigarette.

139.speaker: Estela Toras
139.text: "You do realize that she'll be nothing but a liability to you in that room."

140.speaker: Estela Toras
140.text: "You made the right decision. In that room, she's nothing but a liability to you."

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "I just don't want her concerning herself with state affairs at such a young age."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "It doesn't matter either way. The council is an antiquated institution."

143.speaker: Player_Romus
143.text: "You're right. I don't want to give my opponents any more leverage over me."

144.speaker: Player_Romus
144.text: "You're right. I feel lousy letting her down, though."

145.speaker: Player_Romus
145.text: "I don't care. She's my daughter and she'll get what she wants."

146.speaker: Player_Romus
146.text: "She's the heir apparent. It'll be a good education for her."

147.speaker: Player_Romus
147.text: "One more Toras on the council is an asset, not a liability."

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "What does it matter? The council is an antiquated institution anyway."

150.speaker: Estela Toras
150.text: "Don't let them catch you saying that."

154.speaker: Estela Toras
154.text: "Growing up motherless doesn't give you a free pass forever."

155.speaker: Narrator
155.text: The clock struck quarter to nine. My first council meeting was starting soon.

156.speaker: Estela Toras
156.text: "He always believed you'd make a good king, you know. Even if he didn't always show it."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: I excused myself from the table. As I was leaving the dining room, my mother cleared her throat.

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "I really don't care what my father thought of me."

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: Her laughter followed me up the stairs.

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "I won't just be good. I'll be the best."

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: I headed back upstairs to fetch Vina. It was almost time to go.

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: I headed back upstairs to get ready. It was almost time to go.

172.speaker: Estela Toras
172.text: "Suit yourself. Now, if anyone in this place could make a halfway decent strudel -- *that* would be worth ruining one's figure for."

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: We ate for a while in silence. Vina looked lost in thought. Finally, she spoke up.

174.speaker: Estela Toras
174.text: "We'll make a princess of you yet. Now, if anyone in this place could make a halfway decent strudel -- *that* would be worth ruining one's figure for."

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "Zille will be ours again. And so will Pales."

176.speaker: Estela Toras
176.text: "I never cared much about Pales. But I don't have to tell you how much Zille means to me."

177.speaker: Player_Romus
177.text: "Just two years to go until the treaty expires."

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "Halaita. If it is said, so it is and shall be."

180.speaker: Estela Toras
180.text: "I'll find a suitably scandalizing dress to wear to it."

185.speaker: Vina Toras
185.text: "Right. Silly of me to think you were keeping track."

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: Pabel leveled his gaze at me, his manner calm.

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: He let out a sigh of relief.

188.speaker: Narrator
188.text: The royal bedroom, on the top floor of the residential wing of Palas Rezna, made the one in the Toras palace in Monqiz look shabby. Ornate gold trim covered the walls. I was alone in a bed that could easily have slept four.

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: After I'd left for university, my friend had worked his way up to Chief Butler. It was hard to believe he was now head of my royal household.

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: After I'd left to join the military, my friend had worked his way up to Chief Butler. It was hard to believe he was now head of my royal household.

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: After I'd left for Monqiz, my friend had worked his way up to Chief Butler. It was hard to believe he was now head of my royal household.

192.speaker: Narrator
192.text: In the years I'd been gone, the groundskeeper's son had worked his way up to Chief Butler. I'd seen him on visits to the palace, but we rarely exchanged words. Now, he was the head of my royal household.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: Just then, Vina came bounding down the stairs.

196.speaker: Vina Toras
196.text: "It's unusual for a female heir to join the council, I know. But didn't you do the same when you were my age?"

215.speaker: Pabel Adria
215.text: "Please pardon my impudence. It won't happen again."

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: He drew back the heavy velvet curtains. Sunshine flooded the room.

218.speaker: Pabel Adria
218.text: "Romus Toras, King of Rizia. You've come a long way since we were kids."

219.speaker: Player_Romus
219.text: "Not really. All I had to do to get this job was wait for Father to die."

221.speaker: Player_Romus
221.text: "And yet here I am in the exact same palace."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "It feels natural, somehow. Like I was born to do this."

223.speaker: Pabel Adria
223.text: "Not bad for the groundskeeper's son. Of course, it helped to have friends in high places."

228.speaker: Pabel Adria
228.text: "I know you two didn't get along by the end. But it's never easy to lose a parent."

229.speaker: Pabel Adria
229.text: "I'm so sorry. This must be hard for you."

230.speaker: Pabel Adria
230.text: "But now you've got me as your butler. A significant upgrade from your man in Monqiz, I promise."

231.speaker: Narrator
231.text: He looked me in the eyes.

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "It's complicated. I don't know what I should be feeling right now."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "To be honest, I'm not that bothered."

235.speaker: Player_Romus
235.text: "It must have been even harder being his butler."

236.speaker: Pabel Adria
236.text: "There's no 'should'. You feel what you feel."

237.speaker: Pabel Adria
237.text: "Anything I can do to make your life easier, I'm here."

238.speaker: Pabel Adria
238.text: "Well, I'm here to make your life easier. Let me know if there's anything I can do."

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: Something dark passed across Pabel's face.

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: He briskly drew back the heavy velvet curtains. Sunshine flooded the room.

241.speaker: Narrator
241.text: He gave a brusque nod and drew back the heavy red velvet curtains. Sunshine flooded the room.

243.speaker: Narrator
243.text: He opened the doors of my armoire and began pulling out items of clothing.

244.speaker: Pabel Adria
244.text: "You have quite the packed schedule this morning. Why don't you eat breakfast with the girls while I get your outfit ready?"

248.speaker: Pabel Adria
248.text: "Forgive me if I'm overstepping, but how are you doing? I know you and your father didn't get along by the end. But it's never easy to lose a parent."

249.speaker: Pabel Adria
249.text: "Forgive me if I'm overstepping, but how are you doing? Losing your father must have been hard for you."

251.speaker: Player_Romus
251.text: "I can pick out my own clothes, Pabel."

253.speaker: Pabel Adria
253.text: "Can you? Remember when your father brought the whole family to meet the Baron of Soradis and you insisted on wearing shorts? *Shorts*!"

254.speaker: Pabel Adria
254.text: "Queen Mother Estela and Princess Vina must be waiting already. You should get a move on."

259.speaker: Pabel Adria
259.text: "I ate in the servants' quarters before coming here. There are hierarchies to be observed now that you're king, I'm afraid."

260.speaker: Pabel Adria
260.text: "Don't worry, Your Majesty. I'll make sure you're the best-dressed king in Rizian history."

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: He briskly drew back the heavy velvet curtains. Sunshine flooded the room.

269.speaker: Pabel Adria
269.text: "He had his difficult moments. But I tried my best to make him comfortable in his last days."

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "No, not really. I was thinking about Father."

271.speaker: Player_Romus
271.text: "He can't have been an easy man to serve. Especially towards the end."

275.speaker: Pabel Adria
275.text: "My condolences, Your Majesty. This must not be an easy time."

276.speaker: Player_Romus
276.text: "I have no need for your pity."

278.speaker: Player_Romus
278.text: "Thank you, Pabel. That means a lot."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: Something dark passed across Pabel's face.

282.speaker: Pabel Adria
282.text: "He had his difficult moments. But I tried my best to make him comfortable in his last days."

283.speaker: Pabel Adria
283.text: "Just let me know if there's anything I can do."

285.speaker: Pabel Adria
285.text: "Excuse me. I only wanted to express my sympathies."

286.speaker: Pabel Adria
286.text: "I know you two had your disagreements, but I wasn't aware it was that bad."

290.speaker: Pabel Adria
290.text: "I wasn't aware the two of you were at odds."

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "Hierarchies are meant to be broken. You're the head butler, not a common scullery maid. I insist you join us next time."

294.speaker: Player_Romus
294.text: "Can you at least stop calling me 'Your Majesty'? We don't need to be so formal with each other."

295.speaker: Pabel Adria
295.text: "Always. Bi mare volu, un oxit solu."

296.speaker: Narrator
296.text: I recognized the slogan we'd made up as kids. "Two tides rise, one sun sets."

298.speaker: Pabel Adria
298.text: "I can in private. In public, it would be seen as highly disrespectful."

299.speaker: Pabel Adria
299.text: "I haven't forgotten, though. Bi mare volu, un oxit solu."

301.speaker: Narrator
301.text: Still in my dressing gown, I headed downstairs.

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: He moved over to my armoire and began pulling out items of clothing.

304.speaker: Pabel Adria
304.text: "Why don't you join your family downstairs? I'll have your outfit ready by the time you're finished eating."

306.speaker: Player_Romus
306.text: "I can pick out my own clothes, Pabel."

309.speaker: Pabel Adria
309.text: "I ate in the servant's quarters before coming here."

310.speaker: Pabel Adria
310.text: "This is one of my royal duties, I'm afraid."

311.speaker: Pabel Adria
311.text: "Don't worry, Your Majesty. I'll make sure you're the best-dressed king in Rizian history."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "Can you stop calling me 'Your Majesty'? We don't need to be so formal with each other."

320.speaker: Pabel Adria
320.text: "Queen Mother Estela and Princess Vina must be waiting already. You should get a move on."

322.speaker: Pabel Adria
322.text: "I haven't forgotten. Bi mare volu, un oxit solu."

323.speaker: Pabel Adria
323.text: "Sorry, Your Majesty. But that would be seen as highly disrespectful."

331.speaker: Player_Romus
331.text: "This will be fun. Just like old times."

333.speaker: Player_Romus
333.text: "My grandmother Queen Lyza didn't get her wisdom from serving on her father's council."

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "Greatness is something you're born with, my daughter. You can't glean it off of others."

335.speaker: Player_Romus
335.text: "My grandmother's achievements weren't as noteworthy as everyone says. She just happened to be in the right place at the right time."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "You shouldn't have to worry about living up to anyone's legacy. You're great in your own right."

337.speaker: Vina Toras
337.text: "That's not fair. She was already queen by the time she was my age."

338.speaker: Vina Toras
338.text: "Queen Lyza herself would disagree. That's why she worked so hard to improve educational opportunities for women."

339.speaker: Vina Toras
339.text: "That's what some people say, yes. But I've read all her essays. She was a true visionary."

340.speaker: Vina Toras
340.text: "That's very kind of you, Father. But Lyza was the most beloved queen in our history. Of course people will compare me to her."

341.speaker: Estela Toras
341.text: "You're getting ahead of yourself, sweetheart. The crown is on your father's head right now, not yours."

343.speaker: Estela Toras
343.text: "And what your father needs is for your lovely little face to be seen at balls and ribbon-cutting ceremonies, not hidden behind council doors."

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "Your grandmother's right, Vina. As the princess, it's up to you to serve as the ultimate example of beauty and grace in this country."

345.speaker: Player_Romus
345.text: "Now, Mother. We both know Vina is much more than a pretty face."

346.speaker: Player_Romus
346.text: "That's an outdated image of a princess, isn't it? If Vina wants to get involved in politics, I don't see why I shouldn't let her."

347.speaker: Player_Romus
347.text: "It is true that you'll learn more about how the world works by being out in it, not by shadowing me."

348.speaker: Vina Toras
348.text: "Listen to both of you! I need to learn how to govern the country, not just symbolize it."

349.speaker: Vina Toras
349.text: "Going to balls won't teach me how decrees are made, or how to negotiate with foreign leaders. Only time served on the council will do that."

350.speaker: Vina Toras
350.text: "I do recognize my duty to represent Rizia in public. But I need to learn how to govern the country, not just represent it."

351.speaker: Estela Toras
351.text: "You want to spend the best years of your life cooped up in that den of snakes?"

352.speaker: Estela Toras
352.text: "The council isn't some wise, all-knowing entity. Everyone on it is only looking after their own house and their own stature."

353.speaker: Estela Toras
353.text: "And God help you if you get in the way of either of those."

354.speaker: Player_Romus
354.text: "My councilors represent many cumulative decades of experience. I would not discount their wisdom."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "I have always found it odd that we entrust the country's direction to a handful of privileged nobles."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "My father may have allowed his council to run roughshod over him. I will not make that mistake."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "That's enough, Mother. This is my decision to make."

359.speaker: Estela Toras
359.text: "I'm only trying to be helpful. But you're right, of course. Go on."

360.speaker: Estela Toras
360.text: "Their 'wisdom' turned Pales into a bloodbath and sparked an uprising. It almost got you killed."

361.speaker: Narrator
361.text: Vina looked at me with pleading eyes.

362.speaker: Vina Toras
362.text: "If navigating the council's self-interests will be part of my future duties, I need to learn how to do that too."

363.speaker: Vina Toras
363.text: "If choosing when to ignore the council will be part of my future duties, I need to learn how to do that too."

364.speaker: Vina Toras
364.text: "And besides, if choosing when to ignore the council will be part of my future duties, I need to learn how to do that too."

365.speaker: Vina Toras
365.text: "I promise, it'll be like I'm not even there. And I'll step out in public as much as I can."

367.speaker: Vina Toras
367.text: "I don't know if the uprising was the council's fault. From what I've read, there were many factors."

369.speaker: Player_Romus
369.text: "Honestly, I wasn't even sure what I wanted to say."

370.speaker: Estela Toras
370.text: "But don't let my nattering on keep you from eating. A king needs energy."

375.speaker: Estela Toras
375.text: "I hope it was an apology. He was so cruel to everyone at the end. Not at all like the man I married."

376.speaker: Estela Toras
376.text: "You boys did always have your secrets."

377.speaker: Estela Toras
377.text: "It's a pity he didn't live to preside over my homeland's big return to Rizia. But soon you will."

382.speaker: Estela Toras
382.text: "I don't doubt it, my love. But your father is the one wearing the crown now."

383.speaker: Estela Toras
383.text: "That's true, sweetheart. But your father is the one wearing the crown right now. Not Lyza, and not you -- yet."

384.speaker: Estela Toras
384.text: "Her Majesty loved women, yes. Except for the one her son married."

385.speaker: Estela Toras
385.text: "In any event, sweetheart, your father is the one wearing the crown right now. Not Lyza, and not you -- yet."

386.speaker: Vina Toras
386.text: "It would mean the world to me, Father."

387.speaker: Estela Toras
387.text: "Because I didn't want you holed up in there all the time. A grandmother's got to see her granddaughter every so often, you know."

389.speaker: Player_Romus
389.text: "I insist you join us at the table next time. You're the head butler, not a common scullery maid."

391.speaker: Pabel Adria
391.text: "If the King commands it, I can hardly refuse."

393.speaker: Player_Romus
393.text: "Even more fashionable than King Darius the Debonair?"

395.speaker: Pabel Adria
395.text: "I wasn't aware such a monarch existed. But yes, I'll do my best."

396.speaker: Player_Romus
396.text: "How rude. In the future, you will not take a bite before your King does."

398.speaker: Pabel Adria
398.text: "Of course, Your Majesty. I'll see to it."

401.speaker: Pabel Adria
401.text: "If the King commands it, I can hardly refuse."

402.speaker: Player_Romus
402.text: "Even more fashionable than King Darius the Debonair?"

406.speaker: Narrator
406.text: She looked skeptical for a second, then assumed a reverent position.

407.speaker: Pabel Adria
407.text: "I'm just a humble servant. Enjoy your breakfast."
